title: Machine learning with inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers predicts ICU sepsis
summary: In 1,209 ICU patients from retrospective and prospective multicenter datasets, LightGBM predicted sepsis from first-24-hour data with AUC 87.9% and AUPRC 64.2% on prospective data. Adding IL-6, procalcitonin, CRP and soluble EPCR significantly improved performance (AUC p=4.1e-4). Training data were retrospective, the prospective subset size is not stated, and impact on care is untested; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: LightGBM, random forest, XGBoost, AdaBoost and logistic regression on first-24-hour ICU clinical and biomarker data
organization: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens; Evangelismos Hospital

evidence.tested: Evaluation on prospectively collected multicenter data and biomarker feature ablation.
evidence.unknown: Prospective subset size, clinical impact and generalization; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts which ICU patients will develop sepsis and quantifies the contribution of biomarkers.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations not retrieved. Full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
